parts.title: Reading - Part 3
parts.instructions: For each question, choose the correct answer.
parts.passage_text:
Last month, all the science teachers at my junior high school decided to set up a biology fair. They asked all the students to plan and make a project for the two-day fair last week. I was in a group with my best friends Wei-ling, Julia and Pedro. All the groups worked hard on their projects for two weeks before the fair.

My group did an experiment to find out what happens to your teeth when you drink sugary drinks: we used three eggs because their shells are similar to the outside of our teeth. We put them into different glasses with cola, apple juice and plain water. Then we checked how the colour changed and took pictures that we pasted on a large whiteboard in the hall.

The other groups from my class worked on a lot of interesting projects, too. It was great to walk around the hall and look at the other students while they worked: one group showed how important light is to grow plants. Another group stopped an apple from turning brown by using lemon juice.

We all worked really hard and at the end of the two weeks our teachers chose the top four projects. They gave a prize to each of them. The top prize went to a group of older students. It's a pity that my group didn't get a prize but that's not so important. I was just pleased we took part and we had a great time together.

questions.question: How long did the students prepare for the fair?
What was the main topic of Anita's experiment?

options.A: Apples turn brown when you put them into lemon juice.
options.B: Apples don't change their colour if you use lemon juice.
options.C: Brown apples turn white with lemon juice.

questions.question: How did Anita feel when the teachers chose the best projects?

options.A: angry because her group didn't win
options.B: happy because she enjoyed working with her classmates
options.C: tired because her group had done a lot of work.

parts.title: Listening - Part 2
parts.instructions: For each question, write the correct answer in the gap. Write one word or a number or a date or a time.
parts.context: You will hear a coach telling some boys and girls about a boat race.
parts.transcript:
Hello everybody. I'm going to give you some information about tomorrow's school boat race. All racers must be at the meeting point at ten o'clock because the race will begin at half past ten. All you need to wear is a pair of shorts. You shouldn't wear sunglasses because you may lose them during the race.
Remember that the race is only for students aged 10 to 15. The swimming race for younger children will take place on Friday.
There are different prizes for each race. In the school boat race, for those who win the first prize there is a new surfboard, and those who come second and third will get a book on sailing each. Don't be sad if you don't win, though: everybody who takes part in the race will get a T-shirt as a souvenir.
If you haven't signed up, now just tell me and I will add you to the list.

parts.context: You will hear Nelly and Bart talking about school uniforms.

questions.question: Why have Nelly and Bart not met for a long time?

options.A: He was in a foreign country.
options.C: He was travelling with his Italian uncle.

questions.question: Why is Nelly wearing a school uniform?

options.A: Her own clothes are too old.
options.B: She goes to a different school now.
options.C: Her old school now has a uniform.

questions.question: What does Nelly think about uniforms?
Why doesn't Bart like uniforms?

options.A: He thinks uniforms are too different.
options.B: He thinks everyone looks the same in a uniform.
options.C: He thinks most people don't like uniforms.

questions.question: How does Nelly feel about her clothes?

options.A: She would like to wear them to school sometimes.
options.B: She only wants to wear them on Sundays and Saturdays.

parts.transcript:
Nelly: Hey Bart: I haven't seen you for a long time. Where were you last month?
Bart: Hi Nelly, I was on holiday in Italy with my parents. My uncle Jeff lives there so we stayed at his house. Why are you wearing a school uniform?
Nelly: Well, I can't wear my own clothes any more like at our old school. I changed school last term when I moved to a different part of the town. I told you, didn't I?
Bart: Yes, but I didn't know you have to wear a uniform now. That must be awful!
Nelly: Oh I don't know. It's not such a bad thing, in my opinion.
Bart: But don't you want to wear the clothes you choose?
Nelly: Yes, but… the good thing is that I don't have to think about what I have to wear every morning.
Bart: Well, maybe… but I wouldn't like to wear a uniform anyway. I don't like looking like other people. I want to be different!
Nelly: I don't mind wearing a uniform but I miss wearing my clothes at school sometimes, of course…
Bart: I'm sure you do... but this way you don't need to buy so many clothes anymore. You're right, school uniforms aren't so bad at all!

parts.context: You will hear Elizabeth talking to her friend about a party. What did each of her friends bring?
parts.transcript:
Friend: How was your birthday party, Elizabeth?
Elizabeth: It was great, thanks.
Friend: Did you make a lot of food?
Elizabeth: Not really. I only made strawberries, but my friends brought a lot of things to eat. My favourite was Fred's sandwiches.
Friend: What did Yuki bring? I know she loves making cakes.
Elizabeth: Yes, she does but this time she brought some ice cream because she had no time to cook.
Friend: Oh no! So, you didn't get a birthday cake?
Elizabeth: Of course I did! Leela brought a cake. It was a delicious strawberry cake.
Friend: How about Paul? Did he make his lovely omelettes?
Elizabeth: Yes, and this time he put potatoes in them.
Friend: And Shane? She always cooks rice when there's a party.
Elizabeth: Not this time! In fact, Shane made a salad! I couldn't believe it!
